text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Warri oil refinery in the midwest has been closed since communal clashes there in March and April over the relocation of the local council headquarters, says oil minister Dan Etete.
- A multi-million dollar gas project owned by the joint venture between state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp and Chevron Corp in midwestern Nigeria starts production.
- Recent communal crisis in midwestern oil-producing city of Warri may cause fuel scarcity because of the closure of the oil refinery there, says oil minister Dan Etete.

- Community leaders of Ijaw, one of the tribes involved in the clashes over relocation of their local council headquarters, deny they are members of opposition NADECO group and say their strugle has nothing to do with annulled 1993 presidential poll.
- Two naval officers were mistakenly kidnapped on Friday but released in what would have amounted to a renewal of hostilities in Warri area.
- Share price of First Bank Plc fails to rise despite posting a profit of 1.3 billion naira for last year.
